applies_why: The judge treats the challenger's own chain (1 Chronicles 28:6, Acts 1:8) as footed but resolves the collision by Matthew 1:20's own words, i.e., verse by verse rather than chain against chain by footing.
quote: the challenger's covenant-origin analogy is footed (1 Chronicles 28:6, Acts 1:8) but the sentence's own words state the source of what is in the womb
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: Phrase: weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse. Reading 1: a single verse's explicit statement can resolve the collision; Reading 2: the judge must compare the whole challenger chain's footing against the answering chain and not let one verse decide alone.
why: The judge acknowledges the challenger chain is footed but lets Matthew 1:20's own words decide, which is the verse-by-verse stating-verse approach K-C retires.
